Definition: from G4862 and ἁλίζω (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. convene:--assemble together.
BiblicalUsage: After His resurrection Jesus, being assembled together with His apostles, commands them not to depart from Jerusalem but to wait for the promise of the Father. The waiting begins together, because the promise is given to a gathered people, not to scattered individuals.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God's promises are waited for together, and I hold that the waiting itself is part of the obedience.
